content: 1. The use of progestogen-only pills (POP) for 48 hours is considered necessary to achieve a contraceptive effect on cervical mucus. However, the time required for levonorgestrel (LNG) implants to exert a similar effect remains uncertain. 2. In healthy women, no specific examinations or tests are mandatory before initiating progestogen-only implants. However, it is recommended to measure blood pressure prior to implant initiation, although this is not always feasible in certain settings. 3. Breast examinations, pelvic/genital examinations, cervical cancer screening, routine laboratory tests, hemoglobin tests, STI risk assessments (via medical history and physical examination), and STI/HIV screenings (via laboratory tests) are not essential for the safe and effective use of implants. 4. Blood pressure screening is desirable before implant initiation, but in settings where this is unavailable, women should not be denied access to hormonal contraceptive methods due to the inability to measure blood pressure. 5. The product labeling for LNG implants, such as Implanon, states that the implant can remain in place for up to three years. For Sino-implant (II), the recommended duration is up to four years. 6. Norplant, which has been discontinued since 2008, was originally approved for up to five years of use. However, its contraceptive effectiveness remains high through year seven for women weighing less than 70 kg at insertion and through year four for women weighing 70 kg or more. 7. Women using Norplant who exceed the recommended duration of use may wish to have the implants removed due to an increased risk of pregnancy. 8. For Jadelle, women weighing less than 80 kg can use the implants for up to five years. Women weighing 80 kg or more should consider removal after four years due to reduced effectiveness. 9. The GDG reviewed evidence showing that pregnancy rates among Norplant users are rare through year seven for women under 70 kg and through year four for women 70 kg or more. However, effectiveness decreases significantly for women weighing 80 kg or more after year four. 10. Women using Norplant or Jadelle are at a lower risk of ectopic pregnancy compared to those using no contraception. However, if pregnancy occurs, the likelihood of it being ectopic is increased. 11. Amenorrhea during implant use does not require medical treatment and can be managed with counseling. If unacceptable to the woman, the implant(s) should be removed, and an alternative contraceptive method should be chosen. 12. Spotting or light bleeding is common during implant use, especially in the first year, and is not harmful. Persistent spotting or bleeding, or bleeding after a period of amenorrhea, warrants exclusion of gynecologic problems. 13. For heavy or prolonged bleeding (lasting more than eight days or twice the usual menstrual flow), gynecologic problems should be excluded. If no issues are found, treatment options include NSAIDs or hormonal therapies like combined oral contraceptives (COCs) or ethinyl estradiol. 14. If a woman finds bleeding unacceptable despite treatment, the implant(s) should be removed, and another contraceptive method should be selected. 15. Counseling about potential menstrual abnormalities before implant initiation is essential to address concerns and encourage continued use of the method. 16. No routine follow-up is required after initiating implants. Women should be advised to return if they experience side effects, wish to change methods, or when it is time for implant removal. 17. Progestogen-only injectable contraceptives (POIs) include depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA) and norethisterone enanthate (NET-EN). DMPA is available in intramuscular (IM) and subcutaneous (SC) formulations. 18. DMPA-SC can be administered in the upper arm, abdomen, or thigh, offering flexibility and acceptability for women. 19. A woman can start DMPA-SC within seven days of the start of her menstrual bleeding without needing additional contraceptive protection. If started later, she must abstain from sex or use additional protection for seven days. 20. Postpartum women who are breastfeeding should generally avoid POIs within six weeks postpartum unless no other methods are available. After six weeks, POIs can be initiated if the woman is amenorrheic and primarily breastfeeding. 21. Non-breastfeeding postpartum women can start POIs immediately after delivery or within 21 days without additional contraceptive protection. 22. Women switching from another hormonal method can start POIs immediately if they have been using their previous method consistently and correctly. No additional protection is needed. 23. Women switching from a non-hormonal method can start POIs immediately if it is reasonably certain they are not pregnant. If more than seven days have passed since the start of menstrual bleeding, additional protection is needed for seven days. 24. Women switching from an IUD can start POIs within seven days of menstrual bleeding and have the IUD removed at the same time. If more than seven days have passed, additional protection is required for seven days. 25. The GDG emphasized that counseling and follow-up should address side effects, correct use, and STI protection. Additional assessments may be appropriate based on individual circumstances.
